Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 77, verses 46–49:

Allah's words: ﴿Eat and enjoy yourselves a little; indeed you are criminals.﴾ ﴿Woe on that Day to the deniers.﴾

Know that this is the ninth of the kinds of warning to the disbelievers. It is as if Allah, Exalted is He, says to the disbeliever while he is in this world: "You only exposed yourself to these calamities that We have described and these trials that We have explained because of your love of this world and your desire for its good things and its appetites. However, these good things are few in comparison with those great calamities. The one who busies himself with obtaining them is like one who takes a single morsel of sweets while poison that destroys is within it. It is said to the one who wants to eat it and does not abandon it, despite the advice of the advisers and the admonition of those who admonish: 'Eat this, and woe to you from it after this, for you are among those destroyed by it.'" Although this is in form an imperative, in meaning it is an emphatic prohibition, a great rebuke, and a prohibition in the utmost degree of intensity.
* * *
Then Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Bow down," they do not bow down.﴾ ﴿Woe on that Day to the deniers.﴾

Know that this is the tenth of the kinds of warning to the disbelievers. It is as if it were said to them: "Suppose you love this world and its pleasures; yet do not turn away entirely from serving your Creator, but humble yourselves before Him. For if you believe and then add to that the pursuit of pleasures and various sins, there will remain for you hope of deliverance from the punishment of Hell and of attaining reward, as He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with; but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills.﴾" Then these disbelievers do not do that, nor do they submit to His obedience; they remain persistent in their ignorance and their disbelief, and in exposing themselves to the great punishment. Therefore He said: ﴿Woe on that Day to the deniers﴾, meaning: woe to whoever denies these Prophets who guide them to these interests that combine the good of this world and the Hereafter. Here there are some issues:

The first issue: Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said: as for His words ﴿And when it is said to them, "Bow down," they do not bow down﴾, what is meant is the prayer (ṣalāh), and this is clear, because bowing (rukūʿ) is one of its pillars. Allah, Exalted is He, thus made clear that it is among the characteristics of these disbelievers that when they are called to prayer, they do not pray. This shows that the disbelievers are addressed with the branches of the sharia, and that just as they deserve blame and punishment for abandoning faith, so they deserve blame and punishment for abandoning prayer, because Allah, Exalted is He, blamed them while in their disbelief for abandoning prayer. Other scholars said: what is meant by bowing is humility and submissiveness to Allah, Exalted is He, and that He not be worshipped other than Him.

The second issue: Those who hold that the imperative indicates obligation have used this verse as evidence, because He, Exalted is He, blamed them merely for abandoning what was commanded. This shows that the bare command indicates obligation. If it is said: they are disbelievers, and it is for their disbelief that He blamed them, we say: He blamed them for their disbelief in many respects; however, He blamed them in this verse only because they abandoned what was commanded, so we know that abandoning what is commanded is not permissible.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 77, verse 50:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So in what statement after this will they believe?﴾

Know that when He, exalted is He, had emphatically rebuked the disbelievers from the beginning of this surah to its end, with the ten aspects that we have explained, and urged adherence to reflection (nazar), inference (istidlal) and submission to the true religion, He concluded the surah with a expression of wonder at the disbelievers, and made clear that if they do not believe in these subtle proofs, despite their manifestness and clarity, then ﴿So in what statement after this will they believe?﴾

Al-Qadi (judge) said: This verse indicates that the Qur'an is created (muhdath), because He, exalted is He, described it as a hadith (statement, report), and hadith is the opposite of qadim (eternal), and two opposites cannot coexist; so if it is a hadith, it must not be eternal. The companions (al-Ash'ariyyah) replied: the intended meaning here is these words, and there is no dispute that they are created (muhdathah). And Allah, exalted is He, knows best.

Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and blessings and peace be upon the best of the messengers, Muhammad, and his family, all of them.
